events.title: Only a jump or call reference of the user or the LLM resolves a computed flow, and separate() and the export get the rule from one function: a JMP (N) reads its high byte in the same page, a vector is set by the code's own immediates only when no other write of the code changes it, and their values become reachable targets; an RTS or RTI after pushes is a flow too, with the target of two pushed immediates, else resolved by a jump reference of the idiom pass or the LLM; only a flow in code that a root reaches or that a run executed makes other code unknown; provenance separate lists each code region with reachable, executed and unknown, and the unresolved flows, so its --out file again holds every region, and a cut list of separate or leftovers names the --out file

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Starglider 2 remains byte-exact across 412,736 bytes; six connected disk/media helpers and two shared service-state fields now have bounded roles, while physical-media behavior and minimum Amiga requirements remain open.
change_details.after: Starglider 2 remains byte-exact across 412,736 bytes; loop-wide sparse cells and canonical Dn pointer producers now survive only under proved write envelopes, while an A6 reader remains blocked at a cross-platform call predicate.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.after: Attackwave m68k 2.4.7 now ships a VS Code extension and UAE-backed source debugger, exact 68000 cycle hints, Amiga custom-register diagnostics and decoded Copper views; CI builds tested VSIX packages for Linux x64, Windows x64 and macOS arm64.

events.title: Project metadata updated

events.title: knowledge at takes one or more addresses and answers {revision, addresses}, each address with the access of each coverage map and the joined access; references takes --direction in, out or inside with --range and counts the references by kind and by target; regions counts the regions and bytes of each type; listing --code gives only the instructions; revision counts its rows by kind; coverage takes a recording folder; release keeps the path and the SHA-256 of its file; patch --from-release writes the bytes of a release in the range; and start-screen --capture takes the screen in the program from a capture, with the colours from 1000 bytes of the program or one colour. events.title: The reverse-engineering skill names no file that a script owns: it puts the coverage of each recording into the knowledge, takes the default build and the not-executed count from the result of the generation, and keeps the project layout and the versions of one program in a reference file. The emulator skill drops its filler sections and gives the task to find the instruction that reads or writes an address. c64-basic gives machineCode with the addresses and the file offset of the bytes after the BASIC, and the disk, memory-map, packer and development skills give behaviour in place of mechanics, with the correct symbols file of a build

events.title: The analysis no longer drops a seed in silence: seeds gives the counts that the analyzer got, the counts over its limits, each seed that it did not decode with its reason (outside the program, in data, inside an instruction, into an instruction or data, past the end), and the data ranges that it left out for code. Each coverage gap has its reason, idioms.leftOut gives the idiom tables that another idiom already holds, and writtenNotExecuted lists the analyzer code on bytes that the runs wrote and never executed, with the instructions that reach it, as when an LLM routine led the decompiler into room data. The DXA regions are a list with --max-listed, the summary fields come first, and the skill gives each reason with its action and no longer explains the seeding

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: The Apple IIe/SoftCard environment now exposes kernel-managed W5100 socket and packetless TX/RX APIs, migrates Telnet to the kernel interface and adds a first working WGET client; network execution was not independently repeated.
change_details.after: Zapple-II / BP/M now includes a kernel-backed NETCCP remote-login server with Telnet option negotiation and terminal-independent command output; network execution remains upstream-reported.

before: CP/M Telnet and WGET client integration
after: CP/M Telnet and WGET client integration

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: BO5 is reported 100% for its bounded boss-overlay scope, while the in-tree PC runtime adds most stage overlays and fixes menu/prologue text; upstream explicitly says PC coverage is incomplete.
change_details.after: Castlevania Symphony of the Night decompilation has begun RBO6 boss-overlay asset/entity recovery and corrected Saturn stage-15 sprite/table typing; broader PC and overlay coverage remains incomplete.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Version 0.7.1 adds whole-game m68k-to-C translation roots and overlays, exact display-gap comparison, a web engine and an interrupt-aware Paula state model; upstream reports 2,376 tests, but the tracker did not run them.
change_details.after: amiga-re-kit 0.8.4 fixes long-run CIA timing, A500-style 24-bit/chip-RAM address decoding and CPU-versus-Copper register precedence from Alien Breed II full-game runs.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: v0.10.4 published; packaged demos now open from writable per-user copies, while Windows emulator integration remains explicitly experimental
change_details.after: PiST now analyzes TOS executables with persistent names/comments/code-data marks, live stopped-PC and Hatari coverage notes, picture inspection and source export admitted as a reconstruction only after vasm byte matching.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Primary source reviewed; independent build/run not performed
change_details.after: ND500X documents and indexes the ND-5000 '87 extension: 23 of 25 manual-labelled instructions are represented, with explicit implementation plans and unresolved RHOLE/AMODB scope.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Starglider 2 output remains byte-exact across 412,736 bytes while common airborne and ground launch-state contracts reduce unresolved record accesses from 219 to 207; broader semantics and minimum Amiga requirements remain open.
change_details.after: Starglider 2 remains byte-exact across 412,736 bytes; six connected disk/media helpers and two shared service-state fields now have bounded roles, while physical-media behavior and minimum Amiga requirements remain open.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Wizardry VII reconstruction now routes maze sounds through a recovered semantic C routine; the pinned README reports 271 of 1,099 routines in C (24.7%), with full C conversion still open.
change_details.after: Wizardry VII reconstruction adds named maze/region routines and derives typed data-file layouts from C declarations and recovered records; the pinned README still reports 271 of 1,099 routines in C (24.7%).

before: semantic C replacement under assembly comparison
after: semantic C replacement under assembly comparison

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Authenticated Nexus evidence now carries a retained retail BKR through Continue into a four-champion dungeon view, while FM Towns DM2 traces cover startup source frames; Firestaff-side Continue loading, HUD/viewport and presentation parity remain unimplemented or unverified.
change_details.after: Firestaff now hash-locks four authentic DM1 SNES cartridge images, decodes both H03 ROMDUNGEON slots and validates their shared 14-map structure; native SNES runtime, rendering, input and audio remain out of scope.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Primary source and build workflow reviewed; independent execution unverified
change_details.after: DCTelnet now builds with m68k-amigaos GCC 16.2, and its GCC binary restores cursor-key navigation in the shell and Mystic BBS by correcting signed CSI-byte handling.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Active Rust/C++ Amiga disk toolkit; decoded views now cover Workbench icons and indexed, EHB, HAM and 24-bit ILBM images with upstream corpus accounting and fuzz-bounded allocation checks.
change_details.after: Amiga Disk Engine now follows executable control flow into functions, cross-references and call graphs, names proven library calls, and exports source that GNU as rebuilds byte-for-byte across 39,363 corpus programs.

change_details.before: Working Win32 reconstruction and SDL2 port; the scramble/cutscene change now matches the original register allocation byte for byte, while the remaining strict-byte runs and whole-project completion stay open.
change_details.after: MAIN message functions now use standard varargs while the full 518,656-byte executable and mandatory hash remain exact; two instruction-value checks cover 1,550 functions, with documented declaration and qualifier blockers still open.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Scoped PC-98 reconstruction now accepts 33 OP extents / 32 procedures / 4,370 owned bytes, including 487 initialized DATA bytes with actual-consumer and mutation contracts; whole-product source/link ownership remains open.
change_details.after: MAINL gains source-present DOS exception throw and global-unwind recovery covering 2,524 original bank bytes, but adds zero exact bytes; candidate size, EFLAGS and whole-TU gaps remain explicit.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: 1995 DOS source with modern compatibility layer and Zig build recipes. README distinguishes compilation success from incomplete SDL/audio and potentially crashing stub runtime.
change_details.after: The preserved 1995 DOS source now ships playable Linux, Windows x64, macOS and web ports plus a compatible level editor; differential fuzzing also corrected the documented same-turn arrow/glass rule.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Primary source reviewed; independent build/run not performed
change_details.after: Original Oric Atmos homebrew now shares one IVM bytecode generator and printer between its TPI compiler and parser, with constant-pool, accumulator and bounds checks consolidated in the same implementation.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Primary source reviewed; independent build/run not performed
change_details.after: Original Z80 development tooling now includes a headless CyborgOS platform alias and pause/state services; upstream compared 954 generated programs and platform outputs without changes outside the new platform scope.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Primary source reviewed; independent build/run not performed
change_details.after: ND100X adds a disk-image CPU-identity editor that resolves SINTRAN symbols and segment pages from the mounted pack, ejects before patching, verifies the stored image and remounts it; upstream reports 37 focused checks.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Starglider 2 output remains byte-exact while six projectile-creator call contracts and their storage roles are restored; 24 orphan layout coordinates were removed, but broader semantics and minimum runtime requirements remain incomplete.
change_details.after: Starglider 2 output remains byte-exact across 412,736 bytes while common airborne and ground launch-state contracts reduce unresolved record accesses from 219 to 207; broader semantics and minimum Amiga requirements remain open.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Source reviewed; upstream build and fidelity claims qualified
change_details.after: Wizardry VII reconstruction now routes maze sounds through a recovered semantic C routine; the pinned README reports 271 of 1,099 routines in C (24.7%), with full C conversion still open.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Apple IIe 6502/Z80 SoftCard environment; current source fixes CP/M file truncation and directory search, caches terminal personality for faster output, and makes tab switching interrupt DIR/TYPE. Independent build/run not performed.
change_details.after: The Apple IIe/SoftCard environment now exposes kernel-managed W5100 socket and packetless TX/RX APIs, migrates Telnet to the kernel interface and adds a first working WGET client; network execution was not independently repeated.

after: CP/M Telnet and WGET client integration

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Dreamcast SH-4 decompilation now reports 98.3% of C-capable functions, 90.8% of eligible code bytes and 64.7% aggregate instruction coverage, with 57 functions left after seven newly proven functions and reader/repair fixes.
change_details.after: Dreamcast SH-4 decompilation now reports 99.5% of C-capable functions, 97.8% of eligible code bytes and 70.6% aggregate test coverage, with 18 of 3,299 C-capable functions and 17,086 eligible bytes left.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: ZX Spectrum disassembly now underpins v1.1.0 distribution builds for Aquarius+, Z88, Mitsubishi Multi 8, PC-8801 and SAM Coupé; tracker-side build/run not performed.
change_details.after: The shared Z80 reconstruction adds scenario disasters, square minimaps for PC-88 and Multi 8, and Aquarius+ 4bpp minimap plus text-layer menus, dialogs, budget and evaluation screens; Aquarius+ display details remain hardware-unverified.

before: shared simulation with platform-specific display, input, sound and file layers
after: shared simulation with platform-specific display, input, sound and file layers

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: PAL 2.00 PlayStation 2 matching reconstruction; the hero refactor types sound slots and draw queues and removes overlay-private hero structures, while matching and playability remain upstream work in progress.
change_details.after: PAL 2.00 PS2 reconstruction now shares typed LevelState/camera, render, pause, particle, puzzle and memory-card structures across overlays; these structural refactors do not by themselves establish additional matching or playability.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: The scoped DOS real-mode p-code view recovers 15 additional C decompilations across six builds (3,460/3,468 versus stock Ghidra's 3,445/3,468) and verifies a bounded renderer ownership block; whole-renderer and gameplay parity remain open.
change_details.after: Six-image DOS analysis now fixes the 55,015-byte save-slot layout, exercises caller/blitter contracts in 4,536 cases, and traces the default viewport split chain in 492 cases; runtime reachability, VGA output and whole-game parity remain open.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Source reviewed; upstream build and fidelity claims qualified
change_details.after: The reconstruction now records three passing Xtensa firmware profiles with exact size budgets and an original-ROM oracle with 14/14 scalar STRING cases observed twice; device execution and broad BASIC compatibility remain explicitly unverified.

after: three-profile Xtensa size and ABI verification

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Firestaff now rescans authenticated game data after folder access is granted or repaired, keeping launcher access ownership separate from the runtime; full campaign and presentation parity remain open.
change_details.after: Authenticated Nexus evidence now carries a retained retail BKR through Continue into a four-champion dungeon view, while FM Towns DM2 traces cover startup source frames; Firestaff-side Continue loading, HUD/viewport and presentation parity remain unimplemented or unverified.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: active; current main drives an Ameristar A2065 on physical Amiga 3000 hardware; no independent local build/run
change_details.after: AmiNetXDuo now pins reviewed NetX Duo TCP corrections for FIN acknowledgement, recovery boundaries/timers and DATA/FIN SACK recovery; the existing physical A3000/A2065 profile remains the only measured tracker runtime profile.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Early Amberstar reimplementation now integrates fight-or-flee choice, encounter triggering, battle outcomes, loot, defeated-monster removal and rescue/game-over handling; no complete-game claim.
change_details.after: Amberstar framework now loads English Amiga data, reproduces Amiga outro pictures/copper gradients and handles Amiga COSO/TFMX music and samples, including the seven-voice outro path; complete-game parity is not claimed.

change_details.before: Dreamcast SH-4 decompilation; upstream reports 95.7% of C-capable functions, 87.6% of eligible code bytes and 65.5% aggregate instruction coverage, with 176 functions left.
change_details.after: Dreamcast SH-4 decompilation; upstream reports 95.7% of C-capable functions, 87.6% of eligible code bytes and 65.5% aggregate instruction coverage, with 176 functions left. Reader/repair tooling now handles dominator trees, shifted call indexes, call answers, hidden pointers with register arguments and frame words above stack copies.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Dreamcast SH-4 decompilation; upstream reports 96.5% of C-capable functions, 77.3% of eligible code bytes and 54.8% aggregate instruction coverage, while retaining 114 functions left.
change_details.after: Dreamcast SH-4 decompilation now reports 98.3% of C-capable functions, 90.8% of eligible code bytes and 64.7% aggregate instruction coverage, with 57 functions left after seven newly proven functions and reader/repair fixes.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Source reviewed; upstream build and fidelity claims qualified
change_details.after: The Amiga data set's entrance now follows Dungeon Master Amiga 3.6 timing: two-pixel door steps every 40 ms and a period-79 rattle every 0.8 s, with regression checks distinct from the Atari/CSBWin path.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Pharo-hosted Smalltalk-80 VM now implements and documents native primitive 103 text scanning with a guarded guest-code fallback; independent execution was not performed.
change_details.after: Pharo-hosted Smalltalk-80 VM corrects 32-bit positive-integer conversion between guest objects and the host, including little-endian LargePositiveInteger values up to four bytes; independent execution was not performed.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: In-progress PlayStation matching decompilation; current work deobfuscates collision triggers across all supported regional symbol maps without establishing a complete playable reconstruction.
change_details.after: In-progress PlayStation matching decompilation; current work deobfuscates shared character-collision structures and routines across bodyprog, player control, combat and multiple map actors without establishing complete playability.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Development head adds whole-machine SHA-256 state fingerprints, frame-boundary keyboard/joystick serialization, non-stalling plotter scheduling and configuration-relative RAM-disk backup handling.
change_details.after: Sharp MZ emulator/debugger now returns replay-seek run identifiers for reliable stop waits and hardens parallel testing so all built MZ-800/700/1500 binaries are exercised without oversubscribing shared MSYS Git/Bash resources.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Source reviewed; upstream build and fidelity claims qualified
change_details.after: The scoped DOS real-mode p-code view recovers 15 additional C decompilations across six builds (3,460/3,468 versus stock Ghidra's 3,445/3,468) and verifies a bounded renderer ownership block; whole-renderer and gameplay parity remain open.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Source reviewed; upstream build and fidelity claims qualified
change_details.after: Riptide 0.20 packages the faster GCC build, requests ECN on outgoing TCP connections and extends the Amiga tools test so loopback connections exercise ECN; runtime minimums remain undocumented.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Source reviewed; upstream build claims qualified in notes
change_details.after: Multi-format Acorn disk editor now detects and refuses Acorn Z80 CP/M images whose locked $.CPMDISC catalogue placeholder masks the CP/M filesystem, directing those images to CP/M Disk Wrangler to prevent destructive DFS writes.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Source reviewed; upstream build and fidelity claims qualified
change_details.after: Android reconstruction now includes a campaign core-reserve deployment phase and corrected sea-transport movement/disembark behavior; broader campaign parity remains under active reconstruction.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: active cross-platform Ambermoon reimplementation; the Ambermoon DC mod now has a release workflow, data-driven multilingual quest definitions, code-extension hooks and save-backed quest progress, with manifest/assets/theme and 60 generated-floor tests rather than a new base-engine compatibility claim

last_commit.message: NFS_DOS.EXE of EA's 1997 CD accepted too (a player's: "not the version ReNFS knows"). Its build, dated 17 June 1996, the same 1,254,591 bytes, differs from the 19 June one laid out and relocated only in the give-up branch of keys_control_word 0x48bec (the word written 0x000087a0, not 0xffff87a0; the function 4 bytes longer) and one German text at 0xe3814, neither read by the port: exe.c takes either FNV-1a (0x76078ed2, 0x21ef7c33). With every read checked against those bytes, the 1997 CD drew the same pictures in the front end, the four replays (equal at every snapshot) and nine races. Our CD copy has three bits flipped where the 1997 CD's bytes match their neighbours (NOTES §1). The message no longer says 1996.

change_details.before: Dreamcast SH-4 decompilation with region-pinned rebuild and function-equivalence workflow; upstream reports 60.1% of C-capable functions and 23.3% of eligible code bytes complete, with 13.2% aggregate instruction coverage
change_details.after: Dreamcast SH-4 decompilation; upstream reports 95.7% of C-capable functions, 87.6% of eligible code bytes and 65.5% aggregate instruction coverage, with 176 functions left.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Dreamcast SH-4 decompilation with disc-driven reconstruction and C-equivalence workflow; upstream reports 93.9% of C-capable functions and 66.4% of eligible code bytes complete, with 45.9% aggregate instruction coverage
change_details.after: Dreamcast SH-4 decompilation; upstream reports 96.5% of C-capable functions, 77.3% of eligible code bytes and 54.8% aggregate instruction coverage, while retaining 114 functions left.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: DOS reconstruction playable; native x64 path now has source-bound PC-98 keyboard/UART repeat and stalled-receiver oracles while whole-picture and physical timing remain open
change_details.after: PC-98 reconstruction plus a downloadable Windows x64 preview; upstream documents Normal/Extra, ending/name/save and Music Room checks while complete DOS pixel/timing and physical-sound identity remain open.

before: PC-98 keyboard and UART oracle comparison
after: PC-98 keyboard and UART oracle comparison

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Primary source now includes seedable deterministic weak-bit and not-ready-drive noise for reproducible floppy-controller tests; independent build/run not performed.
change_details.after: Active classic-Mac emulator/debugger; current M68k work corrects exception-frame PCs for long divide-by-zero and FTRAPcc and adds focused format-2 frame tests.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Active multi-system emulator; Mega Drive is now included in the default build and upstream reports a number of games playable, while the README machine list is not yet updated.
change_details.after: Multi-system emulator with default Mega Drive support; current code parses ROM headers and adds battery-backed SRAM load, mapping, access control and save-file synchronization.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Work in progress; snapshot saving now coordinates interpreter-linked object memory, garbage-collection roots and host file operations
change_details.after: Pharo-hosted Smalltalk-80 VM now implements and documents native primitive 103 text scanning with a guarded guest-code fallback; independent execution was not performed.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: In-progress PlayStation matching decompilation; current collision work replaces opaque shape handling with typed polygon/cylinder structures and clearer pass-state logic; no independent build or execution
change_details.after: In-progress PlayStation matching decompilation; current work deobfuscates collision triggers across all supported regional symbol maps without establishing a complete playable reconstruction.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Early matching project with actor/base sources. README explicitly says it cannot compile to a full ROM yet; do not imply a playable reconstruction.
change_details.after: Early Nintendo DS matching project that still does not build a full ROM; current Object317 recovery adds resource loading, selection state, input handling and an actor profile but retains an incomplete render path.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Active PlayStation source reconstruction: upstream reports 246 complete function contracts, 119 unchanged normal ELFs, and a 299,819/299,819 reconstructed-image comparison while explicitly retaining unresolved source/SYM/SLD work.
change_details.after: Active PlayStation matching reconstruction; current work replaces ad-hoc EACPSXZ declarations with canonical library headers while wider source/SYM/SLD recovery remains incomplete.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Active source-only v1.9.2 native Mega Drive port; fixes early-hit boss invulnerability and wrapped Round 3 arena arrivals
change_details.after: Source-only v1.9.5 native Mega Drive port; restores Round 5/7 dialogue scenery, snake poison, falling-rock sound and used bonus-door persistence, with physical hardware still untested.

events.title: Project metadata updated

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Working Win32 reconstruction and SDL2 port; upstream reports 516,228 of 518,656 strict-matching bytes (99.5319%) with 2,428 differing positions in 565 runs, while current navigation/expression probes remain deliberately unretained.
change_details.after: Working Win32 reconstruction and SDL2 port; upstream now reports 517,025 of 518,656 strict-matching bytes (99.6855%), leaving 1,631 differences in 264 runs while all 1,539 mapped functions retain their addresses.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Systemless 0.100.0 extends its classic-Mac PowerPC runtime with CFBundle/CFURL FSRef conversion, native fixed-function OpenGL 1.2 presentation and additional CoreFoundation getters; established Warcraft II playability remains an upstream claim.
change_details.after: Systemless 0.100.0 remains the published baseline; development head now implements QuickDraw AngleFromSlope for PowerPC applications with signed fixed-point edge-case tests through the PEF import path.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Incremental DOS C reconstruction still reports 286 strict routines among 331 identities; its native boundary audit now requires exact intermediate FLAGS witnesses and independently rejects a wrong-CS and ADD-assignment mutant without establishing whole-game completion.
change_details.after: Incremental DOS C reconstruction still reports 286 strict routines among 331 identities; current native fixtures record DOSBox-X executable provenance for bounded 128-case RES03F1/RES0464 comparisons without adding recovery credit.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Source reviewed; upstream build claims qualified in notes
change_details.after: Byte-exact Amiga disassembly/rebuild plus enhanced branch; upstream now reports WinUAE tests for the corkscrew scroller, 48 KiB mirror cache and 50 Hz presentation, while real-hardware validation remains open.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Starglider 2's generated catalogue now projects 2,741 native app references with explicit base provenance while preserving byte-identical C/vasm output and all 57 assets; byte ownership and remaining semantics are unchanged.
change_details.after: Starglider 2 output remains byte-exact while a canonical common-prefix join restores six typed XYZ projections, reducing unresolved record accesses from 277 to 271; broader semantics remain incomplete.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Substantial desktop Sega machine/peripheral emulator; Windows package is described upstream as ready to run, with fidelity unverified here.
change_details.after: Desktop SG-1000/SC-3000/SF-7000 and related emulator/debugger; MSX1 support now includes two joysticks, logical cartridge breakpoints and ASCII 16 MegaROM banking while other MegaROM mappers remain unsupported.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Source inspected; no independent build or execution
change_details.after: USA PlayStation matching reconstruction; stage data now delegates per-area map, image, music and object rows to room instances while upstream reports a clean matching build.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Development head now decodes native DM1 FM Towns GRAPHICS.DAT RLE assets and verifies shipped 320×200 asset output plus authenticated DM2 Towns HUD portraits; broader cross-game presentation and gameplay parity remain open.
change_details.after: Firestaff v3.0.416 and current head add bounded authenticated launcher, Theron and cross-platform startup evidence while explicitly limiting picker coverage to available media and leaving full campaign/display parity open.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: v2.3.0 published with reconstructed dform plus DOS-derived dcopy/dcomp utilities; independent rebuild and runtime verification remain unperformed
change_details.after: Reconstructed CP/M-86 kernel and command distribution; HDMAINT source has been added, while GENDEF now has an explicit analysis record and remains a shipped binary with source reconstruction deferred.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Active partial Rust/C++ Amiga disk toolkit with upstream-reported Linux CLI/Qt operation; format coverage is uneven and some README statements are stale.
change_details.after: Active Rust/C++ Amiga disk toolkit; decoded views now cover Workbench icons and indexed, EHB, HAM and 24-bit ILBM images with upstream corpus accounting and fuzz-bounded allocation checks.

The stage's C includes them as two runs (spawns_1: 14 rooms; spawns_2: the landing pad's, after its object places), its five object kinds are gone with the tables, and the 16 owner= lines naming those tasks and models leave its symbol map. events.title: A room's, an actor's and the stage's generated C is one include per run, not one per module with ROOM_PART selecting a part: a run is a module's objects that follow each other in a unit with nothing else between them, written as <module>.inc, or <module>_1.inc, <module>_2.inc in address order where other data or a unit boundary interrupts the module, and the declarations as declarations.inc, or declarations_<unit>.inc per unit; the build generates the runs the overlay's sources include, so a source naming a run that is not there fails it. The 75 ROOM_PART selectors in 23 rooms' and the stage's sources are the runs they selected. The area objects' place lists are a module of their own (object_places) beside the object table (objects), so the stage's objects are object_places_1, objects and object_places_2. sync-c writes the runs, finds a stage's source (src/stages/<stage>/stage.c) and a room's units by their declarations include (it missed the MIST rooms, under mist_<room>/). events.title: The Akropolis map is assets: its two pages are packages of the group rooms/akropolis/map (page_1, mappic_s1_00, which map files 30100 and 30101 load; page_2, mappic_s1_02, file 30102), loaded into the PE slot, whose 16 room shapes are declared untextured models with bindings, placed whole and exported under their C symbols. The stage overlay binds both pages, and its shape table names each shape through the page its row names (package.map_page_file_id: 30000 + 100 x stage + page), as map_page_1.square and so on, which its C writes as &gMappicS100SquareShape (was (void*)0x8012EFD8); the pages' C includes the generated models (with their footprint comments). The pages' 32 model objects leave overlays.toml and the stage map's 16 owner= lines its symbol map; the legacy records of the two packages and of the seven shapes only they held leave asset_data.py (ratchet 4833 ASSETS, 580 EMBEDDED_ASSETS). The other map pages' raw shape includes are named by order among the versions of each shared stream, so with page 1's versions gone six of their names changed, which six page sources follow (mappic_s2_00, s2_02, s3_00, s3_02, s4_00, s4_02). package.file_ids lists every file holding a package. A clean build matches

events.title: The Akropolis stage's packages declare their models and collision only as assets: overlays.toml loses the 460 model, model source, animation, collision grid, header and patch objects of the 68 entries for its rooms, the MIST's and every package they bind (with those entries' other packages, which share their objects), and the build takes them from the packages' declarations instead. Every model there is a declared model, and the 115 copies no package placed yet are placed now (arrays to TmdSource record); the 25 grids beside the square's are collision assets placed by their rooms, each with its cell_face_list_macro (the square's too), and No. 9's and the lesser Stranger's patches are collision assets with their pieces. package.placed_models and placed_collisions list what packages place as the build's rows, and gen_overlay_configs' declared_models, declared_collisions and declared_collision_patches add them to the manifest's (which still wins where it declares an object); the room tools take a grid's face-list binding from its asset, and the build checks a grid's placement ends where its header begins. Every animation run there was a declared clip already. Generated includes and splat configs are byte-identical

events.title: Code references between stage-1 packages are exports too: the shooting gallery (29: its functions Pierce calls, its task tables, the targets' models), the plaza (35 police clips), the cafeteria (its scene tasks), the cafeteria Stranger (5 clips the boss plays), the MIST parking, the square, the landing pad (No. 9's spark line and vibration) and the fire escape (the lesser Stranger's collision grid) export 78 names, and the 9 actors naming them require those packages. A package's link takes every export of the packages it binds or requires (package.link_symbols; where two give one symbol different addresses, the one its data names), written by gen_overlay_configs.py as absolute symbols into the overlay's generated symbol map, so splat names them in its output and the link imports them; ninja_config writes no export files of its own. tools/check/check_exports.py, run by the unscoped build, holds each of the 216 exports to its own package's linked image (defined there, at its slot address plus at). The banks' borrows field is gone: a bank binds clips from the packages its package binds or requires, which now covers the police and the cafeteria boss. The 79 absolute lines the exports replace leave the 9 actor maps. The sucklerceph packages' references into Shelter rooms stay, waiting on imports

events.title: The Akropolis stage overlay is a package: it loads into the stage slot, requires gameplay and exports the 63 placement tables its rooms' area variants point to (patio_variant_1_placements, ...). The rooms' data names them as rooms/akropolis/stage.<export>, through the stage they require, and their C writes the array bare (gMapAkropolisPatioVariant1Placements, was (void*)&gMapAkropolisPatioVariant1Placements). Decoding names a pointer into a required package by its exports (package.required_exports), and a room of a stage that is a package no longer reads the stage's own names from its symbol map, only the lines that map gives for the room itself; the decoded rooms are unchanged but for those 63 references. The build's export symbols cover required packages as well as bindings, and the 63 owner=map_akropolis lines leave the room maps, with the fountain's stale gActor101100Tasks (it binds the recolored brute, whose table is gActor01100Tasks)

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Primary source reviewed; independent build/run not performed
change_details.after: The current source reports 283/283 DOS entry roles (100%), 174/336 Windows roles and 55/80 Mac jump-table roles with lossless byte coverage; CD-i reconstruction was removed from the current tree and full gameplay/platform equivalence remains unverified.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: 403 exact MAIN functions / 65,198 exact owned bytes and 97.54% reviewed MAIN CODE; ZUN launcher and transfer source scopes plus OP renderer/sound scopes are now accepted without a whole-game completion claim.
change_details.after: Scoped PC-98 reconstruction now accepts 33 OP extents / 32 procedures / 4,370 owned bytes, including 487 initialized DATA bytes with actual-consumer and mutation contracts; whole-product source/link ownership remains open.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Active classic-Mac API runtime; upstream now records native PowerPC Warcraft II campaign play alongside Carbon File Manager, SoundSprocket and MathLib compatibility work.
change_details.after: Systemless 0.100.0 extends its classic-Mac PowerPC runtime with CFBundle/CFURL FSRef conversion, native fixed-function OpenGL 1.2 presentation and additional CoreFoundation getters; established Warcraft II playability remains an upstream claim.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Incremental DOS C reconstruction reports 286 strict routines and 331 identities; a new fixup-backed far-call enumerator supports bounded overlay-stub identity arguments without establishing whole-game completion or playability.
change_details.after: Incremental DOS C reconstruction still reports 286 strict routines among 331 identities; its native boundary audit now requires exact intermediate FLAGS witnesses and independently rejects a wrong-CS and ADD-assignment mutant without establishing whole-game completion.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Active PS1 emulator/debugger: current source adds tested NTSC 480i DFE row suppression, SPU-mix WAV capture, safer legacy save-state GPU restoration and correct Lua breakpoint labels; independently unbuilt and unrun
change_details.after: Active PS1 emulator/debugger now models CD-ROM pickup, spin-up, Init, Pause and GetID timing from SCPH-7001/9002 measurements and applies NTSC 480i DFE row suppression in both software and OpenGL GPU paths; independently unbuilt and unrun.

events.title: Project metadata updated

before.name: Tang Nano 20K SMD variant
before.notes: Upstream's measured fast20 configuration with SMD and tape reader uses 89% logic and 45 of 46 BSRAM blocks, routes successfully, and boots SINTRAN from 21540& in 26 seconds. This is a verified board/build combination, not a minimum FPGA or memory requirement.

evidence.excerpt: SMD + tape reader ... routed; 21540& boots SINTRAN in 26 s

before.name: Tang Nano 20K Winchester default
before.notes: Upstream reports the default Winchester plus tape-reader build at 87% logic and 45 of 46 BSRAM blocks, routed and booting SINTRAN from 20500&. SMD and Winchester together do not route on the tested Tang configuration.

evidence.excerpt: Winchester + tape reader (the default) ... routed; 20500& boots SINTRAN

after.name: Tang Nano 20K SMD variant
after.notes: Upstream's measured fast20 configuration with SMD and tape reader uses 89% logic and 45 of 46 BSRAM blocks, routes successfully, and boots SINTRAN from 21540& in 26 seconds. This is a verified board/build combination, not a minimum FPGA or memory requirement.

evidence.excerpt: SMD + tape reader ... routed; 21540& boots SINTRAN in 26 s

after.name: Tang Nano 20K Winchester default
after.notes: Upstream reports the default Winchester plus tape-reader build at 87% logic and 45 of 46 BSRAM blocks, routed and booting SINTRAN from 20500&. SMD and Winchester together do not route on the tested Tang configuration.

evidence.excerpt: Winchester + tape reader (the default) ... routed; 20500& boots SINTRAN

after.name: MEGA65 R6 OPCOM bring-up
after.notes: Upstream reports the R6 whole-machine core running on a tester's physical MEGA65: a 20 MHz ND-120 configuration with 4 MB configured main memory boots to OPCOM and drives the native 640x480 console. SINTRAN was not yet tried on this board, R3 was not run, and the configuration is not claimed as a minimum.

evidence.excerpt: R6 boots to OPCOM on a tester's machine ... 20 MHz ... 4 MB ... R3 not yet run

change_details.before: Reconstructed ND-120 Verilog system with measured FPGA bring-up: tested Tang Nano 20K SMD-only and Winchester variants boot SINTRAN, while combined SMD+Winchester routing fails on Tang; Nexys and MEGA65 work continue.
change_details.after: Reconstructed ND-120 Verilog system with measured Tang Nano boot profiles and physical MEGA65 R6 bring-up to OPCOM; fresh-clone Nexys DDR2 and nested MEGA65 submodule build gaps are also corrected, while R3 hardware and MEGA65 SINTRAN remain untested.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Starglider 2 semantic restoration preserves complete C/vasm byte equality for the mapped output and reduces unclassified bytes from 25,585 to 22,445; substantial function and field meaning remains unresolved.
change_details.after: Starglider 2's generated catalogue now projects 2,741 native app references with explicit base provenance while preserving byte-identical C/vasm output and all 57 assets; byte ownership and remaining semantics are unchanged.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Development head extends 65C816 recovery through pointer-built JMP/JML dispatch, nested-table cuts and BEQ-guarded nonzero indices, with bounded real-ROM gains and remaining structural over-reads documented.
change_details.after: Development head now recognizes NES inline dispatchers that save Y in absolute RAM and narrows conditional tail calls to genuine entries; bounded Punch-Out!! and SMB3 corpus results improve without treating ROM writes as harmless save noise.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.after: Development head now decodes native DM1 FM Towns GRAPHICS.DAT RLE assets and verifies shipped 320×200 asset output plus authenticated DM2 Towns HUD portraits; broader cross-game presentation and gameplay parity remain open.

events.title: Stage 1's rooms are packages, and every actor they spawn is named through a binding: the other 20 rooms load into the room slot and require gameplay and the Akropolis stage overlay; 17 of them bind the packages their resources spawn (71 bindings with the square's), and 50 more packages export the task tables those name, by the names the room links already used (61 tables in 51 packages; the rat and moth, the officers, the departure, the security monitors and the three sucklerceph and skull stalker packages export one per role). All 95 resource entries that point outside their room now name <binding>.<export> instead of an address (the square's grinning_stranger.task_desc is grinning_stranger.tasks, like the rest); six whose own file is a texture or not on the disc spawn from a package another entry loads, and resolve to the one export of any binding at that address. The build writes build/exports/<room>.txt, each export a room's data references at its package's slot address, and adds it to that room's undefined symbols (a split input); a symbol two bindings give different addresses is an error. package.slot_of finds an actor package in a variant entry's slots too

events.title: A replay of a rebuild with a loader starts the rebuild in the phase of the original at the entry: the replay core holds the rebuild on its first fetch at the entry until the raster beam is where the original had it, and gives it the CIA timers and the interrupt state of the original there (c64run protocol 7, align), as that phase depends on how the original started and a loader can only set the one of the capture; a program that starts its CIA timers without a force load, as Barbarian does, no longer drifts to a false FAIL

events.title: The knowledge keeps the coverage of each map by its project path, as one coverage.jsonl line of ranges for each map and access kind, and the coverage of a space is the union of its maps: a new map of a path replaces the earlier map of that path, so a recording made again into the same folder no longer leaves the code of the old session as executed; coverage gives imported, replaced, known, added and removed, and a coverage.jsonl of an earlier version is refused with the remedy to delete it and import the maps again
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: A deleted or changed file that the knowledge gives as evidence shows at the point of use: docs link lists in evidence each such file with its state and the revisions that give it, by the latest SHA-256 of the file in the knowledge, without a FAIL, and record --out lists each file of the folder that the knowledge gives as evidence and that the record changed, with the hint to import the new coverage.bin, which replaces the map of the earlier recording

events.title: I fixed the MZ-800 state right after a reset. The emulator put the GDG into MZ-700 mode (DMD 08h) and did not map VRAM at 8000h. On the real machine, after power on and after RESET the GDG is in MZ-800 mode (DMD 0, 320x200) and the memory map is the same as after OUT E4h: ROM at 0000h, CG-ROM at 1000h, VRAM at 8000h-9FFFh, ROM at E000h, RAM elsewhere. MZ-700 mode is switched on later by the ROM (OUT CEh with 08h at E816h). This is shown in the MZ-800 Service Manual (pages 6 and 7), and a simulation of the GDG gate-level netlist gives the same map after a cold and a warm reset.

events.title: No. 9 on the landing pad read: the parts both units reach are named from his rig in the private header (pelvis, chest, right forearm, right hand for the sword, left hand for the prop; were BODY_CHEST_PART, WEAPON_PART, PROP_HAND_PART and bare 1/3), the player's splatter lands on Aya's head, and the helipad light's rig names its joints (root, segment_1..9, tip: a ten-segment cable whose tip sparks; the four segments before it draw the spark lines). His clips come from the helipad schemas in place of 31 private ANIM_* constants (the light's, the event's and the player's grenade clips too), his bank 0x78 is SOUND_BANK_NO_9_AKROPOLIS and 23 raw sound ids are SOUND_CHARACTER/SOUND_AREA. The flames draw named cells of the landing pad's sparks page, now declared: flame_*, tongue_*, burning_* and smudge_* (30 cells), with 21 palettes the extractor called unread - smudge on row 270 and the twenty fire palettes on row 271 the tongues and burning flames step through - as its variants; the effect tasks are named for their effects (GolemFlameTask, FlameTongueTask, FlameSpriteTask, GunfireParticleTask, MuzzleFlashTask, ExplosionFireballTask, ImpactBurstTask; were ..Task45, ..4C, ..52, ..59, ..44, ..184, ..185), effect 0x4C is EFFECT_NO9_FLAME_TONGUE, and the gunfire smudge is documented as subtractive (was 'additive'). Docs regain the per-frame flow, the grenade bank's residency, the lap heading lookahead, the lethal strike's one-HP floor, the end-of-lap attack's precedence and the death state's cancel

after.notes: Upstream reports the default Winchester plus tape-reader build at 87% logic and 45 of 46 BSRAM blocks, routed and booting SINTRAN from 20500&. SMD and Winchester together do not route on the tested Tang configuration.

events.title: Every dialogue on the disc decodes (166 of 166): the pipeline follows the second layout tool the game also reads. A decoded dialogue's atlas can state its face (the new bold face dialogue/font_bold), its first_glyph (that tool numbers glyph cells from 0 and has no speaker plates: a title is the glyph cell it draws), and its marks (the ▼ at (242, 242) no cell reaches); MIST room 21's bold glyphs are in cap_glyphs.tsv. Dryfield r04's cells slice across a Japanese page laid out for other text, as the game draws them: they are kept as stored_cells, the text refers to them by cell, and the page is an image of its own (dryfield_r04_glyph_page). CAP_FORMAT.md 9 describes it; 12 no longer lists it

events.title: NFS_DOS.EXE of EA's 1997 CD accepted too (a player's: "not the version ReNFS knows"). Its build, dated 17 June 1996, the same 1,254,591 bytes, differs from the 19 June one laid out and relocated only in the give-up branch of keys_control_word 0x48bec (the word written 0x000087a0, not 0xffff87a0; the function 4 bytes longer) and one German text at 0xe3814, neither read by the port: exe.c takes either FNV-1a (0x76078ed2, 0x21ef7c33). With every read checked against those bytes, the 1997 CD drew the same pictures in the front end, the four replays (equal at every snapshot) and nine races. Our CD copy has three bits flipped where the 1997 CD's bytes match their neighbours (NOTES §1). The message no longer says 1996.

change_details.before: MegaST — Atari ST/STE MiSTery-derived FPGA core for MEGA65
change_details.after: MegaST — Atari ST/STe and Falcon030 FPGA core for MEGA65

before.name: MegaST v1.1 on MEGA65 R6
before.notes: Primary README reports stable real-hardware R6 operation with floppy/hard-disk images, TOS 1.04, named games and additional tester-reported TOS/game configurations. Requires an SD card, tos.img and user media. No 45GS02 requirement or guest ST-RAM size is treated as a host CPU/RAM minimum. v1.1 additionally verifies the read-only internal 3.5-inch drive with an original Jim Power disk.

before.name: MegaST v1.0 on MEGA65 R3/R3A
before.notes: The dedicated R3/R3A core keeps 512 KiB of guest ST RAM in FPGA block RAM because HyperRAM is too slow for cycle-exact timing. Upstream reports R3A operation including hard-disk images. Viking and STEroids modes are unavailable. The 512 KiB value is guest configuration, not host minimum RAM.

after.name: MegaST v1.1 on MEGA65 R6
after.notes: Primary README reports stable real-hardware R6 operation with floppy/hard-disk images, TOS 1.04, named games and additional tester-reported TOS/game configurations. Requires an SD card, tos.img and user media. No 45GS02 requirement or guest ST-RAM size is treated as a host CPU/RAM minimum. v1.1 additionally verifies the read-only internal 3.5-inch drive with an original Jim Power disk.

after.name: MegaST v1.0 on MEGA65 R3/R3A
after.notes: The dedicated R3/R3A core keeps 512 KiB of guest ST RAM in FPGA block RAM because HyperRAM is too slow for cycle-exact timing. Upstream reports R3A operation including hard-disk images. Viking and STEroids modes are unavailable. The 512 KiB value is guest configuration, not host minimum RAM.

after.name: MegaST v1.1.6 Falcon030 test on MEGA65 R6
after.min_cpu: 68030 at 16 MHz guest core; optional 32 MHz turbo
after.os: 512 KiB Falcon EmuTOS or Atari TOS 4.0x; tosfalc.img and fcnvram on SD card
after.notes: Falcon030 is an R6-only test variant. Upstream reports EmuTOS, TOS 4.04, several demos/programs and FreeMiNT 1.19 through text shell/TOS desktop; XaAES remains a white screen. The 4 MiB figure is the lowest explicit guest ST-RAM option, not host RAM.

change_details.before: v1.1 stable; R6 internal 3.5-inch drive support verified read-only; R4/R5 remain untested
change_details.after: v1.1.6 adds a test Atari Falcon030 variant for MEGA65 R6; EmuTOS, TOS 4.04, several demos and FreeMiNT boot, while XaAES and multiple Falcon peripherals remain unverified.

before.name: 512K Lite-client integration
before.os: System 6 with LocalTalk and a MacIP gateway

after.name: 512K Lite-client integration
after.os: System 6 with 128K ROM or later, LocalTalk and a MacIP gateway
after.notes: The v0.1.0 release packages five tools, the TalkIP Driver and AppleTalk On as an 800K HFS disk and StuffIt 1.5 archive. Primary documentation states a Macintosh with 128K ROM or later and 512 KiB RAM, but no minimum CPU is inferred from the machine family.

change_details.before: active; documented Geomys Lite and Flynn Lite 512K integrations
change_details.after: v0.1.0 released: packaged 512K System 6 TCP/IP tools and MacTCP-compatible driver for LocalTalk/MacIP, without MacTCP

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: General PS1 emulator/debugger and development tooling derived from PCSX. Inspected debugger implementation; classify as reusable tooling, not a game-specific emulation port.
change_details.after: Active PS1 emulator/debugger: current source adds tested NTSC 480i DFE row suppression, SPU-mix WAV capture, safer legacy save-state GPU restoration and correct Lua breakpoint labels; independently unbuilt and unrun

events.title: Project metadata updated

before.name: Dot Chase: selected classic 68k build
before.notes: -m68020 build with intuition.library and graphics.library v39, four-plane LORES screen. No PPC branch is evidenced. RAM and chipset minima are unstated; not independently run.

before.name: Fractalus and Void Trader: selected classic AGA builds
before.notes: Both selected builds use -m68020, explicit AGA 320x256x8bpp and v39 OS libraries. No minimum RAM or measured performance threshold is established. 64 KiB stack requests are not RAM minima.

before.name: Fractalus and Void Trader: PPC OS4 variants
before.notes: ARCH=ppc selects -mcpu=440 and newlib with sam460ex/QEMU intent. The PPC variants use silent audio stubs; Fractalus uses graphics.library fallback rendering. Pacing/freezing limitations are author-reported. This does not cover Dot Chase or the whole collection; exact CPU/RAM minimum remains unverified.

before.name: Planet Chomp, Rolling Steel and Spectral Keep: PPC OS4 source ports
before.notes: The three source-level ports are PPC-only and build with ppc-amigaos-gcc -mcpu=440fp/newlib. Planet Chomp and Rolling Steel use OSMesa 7.8.2 software rendering; Spectral Keep renders its precomputed sprites in software. Upstream reports QEMU sam460ex performance, but no minimum physical CPU or RAM requirement is established.

after.name: Dot Chase: selected classic 68k build
after.notes: -m68020 build with intuition.library and graphics.library v39, four-plane LORES screen. No PPC branch is evidenced. RAM and chipset minima are unstated; not independently run.

after.name: Fractalus and Void Trader: selected classic AGA builds
after.notes: Both selected builds use -m68020, explicit AGA 320x256x8bpp and v39 OS libraries. No minimum RAM or measured performance threshold is established. 64 KiB stack requests are not RAM minima.

after.name: Fractalus and Void Trader: PPC OS4 variants
after.notes: ARCH=ppc selects -mcpu=440 and newlib with sam460ex/QEMU intent. The PPC variants use silent audio stubs; Fractalus uses graphics.library fallback rendering. Pacing/freezing limitations are author-reported. This does not cover Dot Chase or the whole collection; exact CPU/RAM minimum remains unverified.

after.name: Planet Chomp, Rolling Steel and Spectral Keep: PPC OS4 source ports
after.notes: The three source-level ports are PPC-only and build with ppc-amigaos-gcc -mcpu=440fp/newlib. Planet Chomp and Rolling Steel use OSMesa 7.8.2 software rendering; Spectral Keep renders its precomputed sprites in software. Upstream reports QEMU sam460ex performance, but no minimum physical CPU or RAM requirement is established.

after.name: Terra Strike: classic 68k AGA build
after.notes: The primary README explicitly states 68020+, AGA and AmigaOS 3.0+ for the classic build. No minimum RAM is stated; the tracker did not run it.

after.name: Terra Strike: PowerPC AmigaOS 4.1 build
after.notes: ARCH=ppc produces terra_strike_os4 with windowed/full-screen graphics and AHI audio. No physical PowerPC model or RAM minimum is stated.

change_details.before: Six substantive game anchors reviewed across classic 68k and PPC AmigaOS variants; independently unbuilt
change_details.after: Seven substantive original/homebrew game anchors reviewed across classic 68k and PowerPC AmigaOS variants; Terra Strike now has a shared-gameplay AmigaOS 4.1 port; independently unbuilt

events.title: Event scripts are room data in a DSL: each stage 1 room's event scripts and the payloads they send (animation requests, actor transforms, actor commands, bank copies, scene keys, walk and move animations) are decoded from the package into <room group>/events.evs (tools/peassets/room/events.py) - payloads declared by kind and name, scripts as one statement per command with only the operands its opcode reads, messages as recipient.message (task slots, scene[i], child[id]) named from event_vocabulary.py (made once from the headers), sound requests by bank, other symbols after & - and read back into the room's objects, encoding exactly. The walk follows a script's operands to its payloads by opcode and message; the record states scripts and the payloads code uses directly as entry points (scripts, animations, transforms, actor_commands, ...). They build into the events module include; the rooms' C loses its event data

events.title: The Akropolis stage's rooms are declared and their data is room assets: every folder of stage 1 (Akropolis and the MIST) is a group under rooms/akropolis or rooms/mist with its chunks named by role (package, bundle, view<N>_background/_image/_palette, sounds_<k>, dialogue_<k>), shared chunks hoisted to rooms/akropolis; the view sprite sheets are 252 page textures and the effect, model, glyph and panorama pages 44 more, placed in new and widened VRAM regions; all 40 room sound banks name their slots; 17 room models and 70 room clips in 15 banks are converted. Each room package is a `room` asset (tools/peassets/room): the extractor walks it from the stage overlay's per-area tables (indexed by area), gameplay's area table and the record's entry points by role (markers, view masks, samples, area updates, vibration scripts, spare sprite batches, alternate light sets and grids, action triggers), decoding every object in the bytes into <group>/room.toml, which encodes back exactly; types follow from roles and the fields that reach them. The build writes one include per module (header, geometry, view boundaries, action triggers, occluders, cameras, sprites, lights, ambient, placements, surfaces, updates, vibrations, markers, view masks, samples) and the declarations (gen_room_inc.py), which the rooms' C includes where each module's block sits; the rooms' C keeps code, code tables, one-off globals and tuning tables, now without const or section attributes on data. The cafeteria's spot-light storage is fifteen spot lights; the stage maps name the per-area tables of all five stages

events.title: The file name of a build tells what it is: without --out, build writes build/release_<label>.prg, build/clean.prg when each value of config.asm is its default, else build/custom_<switches>.prg (no_<name> for a switch that is off), with _<entry> for an entry other than main.asm, and a source without config.asm keeps its entry name; generate --loader writes src/clean_loader.prg (or the custom name) and removes a loader program of an earlier run with another name; the symbols of each build go into symbols/<name>.json beside the program, export too, and --out-symbols is gone

events.title: Port: two of Danik's bugs. From outside, the player's car now faces where it goes: the heading drawn (+0x351) is copied from the heading every step for the racing cars (0x51fa3, race_update_cars), as the original; it was set only on the grid and while paused, so the body kept the grid's heading and turned only in a crash's tumble. After an arrest, the next race no longer has the previous race's colours: the race ends with the ticket still up, and hud_free now lets it go and clears its flag as 0x31bf4 does (the next race's first frame set back the palette saved under it). Reproduced (evening Alpine ended with the ticket up, then midday Alpine) and fixed; a pointer past the opponents' records no longer formed for traffic (opponent.c, UB only). All of tools/checks.sh equal; the CD's four replays equal at every snapshot.

events.title: Port: smooth motion, 60 frames a second (the port's own; NOTES §4.25). The race's steps stay the original's 33.3 a second; each retrace's frame (60 a second at 640x480, 70 at 320x200) is drawn with every car's place, angles and matrix, the camera and the dials set between the last two steps by the fine clock, then put back as the step left it. Jumps are not smoothed (a car put back, the traffic placed, a replay's jump, another camera). On at first; F11 in a race off and on, kept in the home folder's renfs.cfg (the original reads no F10-F12); RENFS_SMOOTH=0|1 for tests. Stepping faster (0x12dd0c) was not the way: the original's faster clocks make the game faster. Checked: the same race off and on leaves the same REPLAY.RPL byte for byte; the CD's four replays equal to all their snapshots with it on; every frame new (without: 2 of 5 repeat), the camera moving evenly; no gaps from inside or outside at both resolutions. README, --help: F11.

events.title: The ending is declared and named: its overlay is ending (was replay_bonus: package, manifest, source, header, symbols, identifiers), its file the ending group - the credits document, a credits shape whose instance is the scroll timing, the eight layout columns and the 417 rows as text in the credits fonts with markup for palettes, columns and pictures, encoding back exactly; the three credits faces (serif, sans, display) as UFOs over a 60-glyph slice each of the document's glyph table on two pages; the font pages' eight color variants, whose palettes the page-0 image stores in its last rows (image chunks may now store palettes in their pages, and a page may hold only palettes) and page 1 an unread copy of; the never-drawn SQUARE and SQUARTZ logos with their palettes; and the credits pictures numbered as the rows name them (picture_0..18; slot 14 is empty and unused). The on-demand death banks are sounds/aya_death and sounds/kyle_death (bank_1..3 each; the game rolls only variants 1 and 2). Declared sounds are written at the rate the game plays them, the octave of 44100 Hz nearest the median pitch every bank's script voices play the sample at (22050 Hz for most), with pitch_keycenter moved to match and the stored root key kept as psx_root_key; and a sound bank names its slots (sounds = { name = slot }, shown in the .sfx) from the C enums and the PE charge table, a sample being a recording and a slot a sound made from it

events.title: Port: a pad drives with the controls left on the keys (Danik: gas, brake and shifting did not work on the controller; his settings had all three on the keys, which the original reads alone, and the automatic starts in neutral). The port's own: with the joystick on, a control on the keys takes the joystick too when none of its keys is held (the steering and pedal values its own kind gives, read as keys), and a pad's right / left shoulder (a joystick's fifth / sixth button) shift up / down whatever the kinds. Only the control word changes: replays and the race record stay the original's. RENFS_INPUT jb5 / jb6. Checked: his settings and calibration with a test pad (neutral without it; the shoulder and the trigger 40 mph, the brake to a stop, the stick steering) and with the Joystick kinds (A shifts, analog steering). tools/replay_stub.c: a joystick stub for the checks; all checks equal. NOTES §4.23.

events.title: Port: the joystick and the mouse for driving (NOTES §4.23). A joystick found at start-up (0x4d1fc: SDL game controllers, the left stick, the right trigger the throttle and the left the brake, A B X Y buttons 1 2 4 8; or joysticks of two axes or more, a keyboard's one-axis device refused), its calibration kept in the home folder's joystick.cfg (0x4d4a0 / 0x4d5ec, the original's 0x5c bytes, equal byte for byte) or made on the calibration screen (fe_joystick_calibrate 0x4c6b0: JOYCAL gold from the menus, JOYCHK green from the race menus; the knob, the pedal bars, Esc leaves it off). The controls screen offers the joystick and mouse kinds and its Calibrate row; without a joystick its kinds go back to the keys (0x39d08). The race's control word by kinds (0x48bec): the joystick's steering and pedals (0x4e0b8), the buttons' pedals and gears, the mouse's steering (0x47b78, relative in a race) and buttons; the horn, handbrake, view (race_keys) and map (hud_keys) on buttons. The stick and buttons in the menus as arrows, Space and Enter (0x4dfe0: fe_read_keys, the text field, the replay bar). RENFS_JOY=1|2 a test stick moved by RENFS_INPUT. Equal to the original in DOSBox with a 4-axis joystick: the calibration screen by palette entry, joystick.cfg, the control words, the controls screen. tools/checks.sh: every check in one command; all equal. nfsdos.py: NFS_DOS_LAUNCHER.

events.title: c64-disk: sectors writes the 256 bytes of the given sectors, then with --unreferenced each used sector that no file holds, into one file and gives the track, sector and offset of each; before, bam listed the unreferenced sectors but nothing read their bytes, and bam now names this command as its nextAction when such sectors exist
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: c64-testing: a record file can say where the coverage of the recording starts, with "coverage": "input" (the default, at the first input read of code in RAM), "start" (when the program starts) or a $ address (at its first execution, also at the pc of a registers step), and the record summary gives coverageFrom with the frame and pc where the map starts, or null, because a map that started after the start-up code made an agent think that game_start and its writes did not run; c64run protocol 3 adds coverage on-pc and coverage status
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: An analyzer reference from a data region of the user, the LLM or a heuristic is false code from packed bytes that the analyzer decoded: the import drops it and counts it in references.inData, the analyzer's own reference from there closes also in a run that is not complete, and a classify of data closes the analyzer references from its range; dual-use bytes keep theirs; before, such references stayed in reference pages and reachability and came back on each run
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: A trace of thousands of hits reaches the caller: the hits go as an attachment of the reply, not in the one message that holds at most 1 MiB, and a result too large for one reply gets limit-exceeded with its size and a remedy and a host log line, not a generic operation-failed; hello and ready also carry the package version, so a client and a host of different releases refuse the handshake and name the older side (a development checkout passes against any release), the protocol version is 5, and after a lost session the MCP server gives that refusal instead of the stored machine-state-lost notice
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: c64-source: a read or a write in the I/O area names the register also where the image holds RAM there (lda CI2CRA, sta RASTER, sta $d800,x for colour RAM without a name, not an offset of the data label at $d000), a platform name in a knowledge operand expression stays as written and becomes a constant in constants.asm, and the RAM keeps its data label without a platform-name label, because a game that copies sprites under the I/O area got every register access written as region+offset; a user or LLM name at the address still wins
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: c64-assembler: an include folder can be anywhere in the project folder, for example build src boot.asm --include ../build for a file that you generated next to the source root: the script stages only the source root and the include folders from the lowest folder that holds them, ACME runs in the source root inside that tree, a diagnostic in such a folder names the file from the source root (../build/tables.asm), and a folder outside the project is refused by name; before, a path with .. was refused and the project folder had to be the source root, which staged the whole project
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: c64-provenance: match keeps the overlapping copies of a routine and names a routine with several copies only at the copy that has the shift of its nearest library neighbours that occur once, or at no copy with an ambiguous reason for each, because the lowest copy was often the wrong one; a $xxxx address in a library comment inside the routine moves by the shift of the match, and a written comment with an address outside the routine is in batch.check for the agent to examine
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: c64-testing: a run file and a scenario name a missing or wrong field with its form (name is a non-empty string, start is a program, a program with load or a snapshot, original and rebuild have program and symbols) and refuse a key that they do not have with the list of their keys, and the run help, SKILL.md and the format reference give the required and optional fields of a run file, because a run file without name failed with "needs a name" and the help did not tell that name is required
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: c64-source: the export rewrite of a scenario gives each side only program and symbols, because a scenario now refuses any other key in original and rebuild and a copied videoStandard made the rewritten scenario fail
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: c64-source: when the check of loader.prg cannot run (the emulator is not available, or another refusal), generate --loader removes the loader.prg that it wrote and gives the normal result with loader.verified false and the reason, and a run without --loader that keeps a loader.asm of another knowledge revision gives staleLoader with the files and a generate --loader nextAction, because an unchecked or stale loader.prg looked like a checked one and a failed check lost the list of written files
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: Port: the race menus' Game options and the audio screen. race_menu_options 0x12760 (CHECK/CHKOPTS.QFS, from both race menus: the finish menu's Options is 0x12760(1), not the chat 0x195d8): Audio, Graphics, Controls, Load and save, Done, Cancel (+9..+0xb4 put back), CONFIG.DAT saved at its end. fe_audio_options 0x105dc from the options screen, the race menus and the pause menu (mode and 3D greyed there): the song (+0x73, the next one heard a second later), the race music's, the menus' music's and the effects' bars (+0x75, +0x77, +0x79; by mouse or Left/Right, heard at once; sound 0x4a over and over on the effects' row), speech, the card's mode (16-bit stereo, 8-bit stereo, 8-bit mono: the mixer's output cut to 8 bits and to one channel; "Changing audio mode" 0x74234), 3D enhanced; Esc and Cancel put it all back. The menus' F5 (0x72638) silences every volume and brings them back; the silence ends before a race, a replay and at the pause menu's end. The menus' music now starts at +0x77 (fe_service_music), the race's at the stream's own. The pointer drawn marks the mouse in use (mouse_draw 0x52288). Equal to the original by palette entry: the audio screen in all three places (DOSBox's 158-pixel scaling strip only), the race menus' options 0 pixels. NOTES §4.2

before.name: Q8 accelerated-emulation qualification
before.notes: Upstream recommends Q8 only above 20 MHz. v1.8.0 reports Turbo6510 64 MHz measurements on public PAL cube scenes: Mode 2 precise/hybrid 23.70/25.05 FPS, Mode 5 27.00/27.45 FPS, and distant-cube Mode 7 standard/fast/fast+LOD 3.10/6.95/11.50 FPS. These are scene-specific emulator measurements, not minima, general guarantees or physical-hardware qualification. The v1.10.2 stable qualification additionally reports Mode 4 stock/turbo results of 0.649958/30.186113 FPS with defaults and 0.749952/38.484510 FPS with arithmetic, camera and visibility experiments; Mode 7 defaults report 0.044442/3.091013 FPS and arithmetic+UV 0.061107/3.703647 FPS. These remain emulator measurements, not physical-hardware or minimum-machine claims.

events.title: DOSBox-X reference runs no longer depend on the workdir path: refrun runs DOSBox-X in the workdir and mounts C: as "c". The shell handles the autoexec mount line in emulated time, so with an absolute path game86's start and every later timer phase moved with the path length (non-monotonic: 121/161/201-char mounts matched the old golden, 41/81/181 not). A fresh clone's deeper build tree failed game_over_hiscore from IRQ 825 and level_50 from 1950 every run (the earlier 'host load' shift was this too; the rerun comment says so now). Goldens regenerated (all 21 runs). Re-fit with per-tick windows: the respawn/wave-start lag (DEVIATIONS #20) now hits level_50 at the wave clear of IRQ 2159 (port a tick behind from 2162: input_shift 2162, divergence pinned at 2250, entities[39]/[41] think_05 llamas on the other parity) and no longer level_30 (identical, shift and pin dropped) or level_50's ~1058 death; level_40_two_player keeps only the 1550 overlay frame pin; level_99 gains frame_phase 2400 (entities[22]+38); level_25_ega unchanged. Independence: regenerated from a shallow workdir, then the full core and long suites from a 259-char-deep one in strict mode (-W error::UserWarning, no rerun): 35 passed / 1 skipped and 26 passed / 1 skipped; a third regeneration from another depth gave byte-identical snapshots (only the two re-fit configs differ)

events.title: W2 fresh-clone findings (lead): (2) every native link warned 'building for macOS-26.5, but linking with dylib ... sdl2-compat ... built for newer version 27.0': Homebrew builds for the running macOS, newer than the Command Line Tools SDK that sets clang's default target. Without an explicit CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET, llama_sdl2 now links for the SDL2 dylib's own minos (LC_BUILD_VERSION via otool), the only systems where it runs anyway (Llamatron's minos 27.0 here). (3) bundle_dylibs.cmake unsigns the executable and each copied dylib (codesign --remove-signature) before install_name_tool edits them, so the 'will invalidate the code signature' warnings are gone; copies are signed ad hoc again afterwards as before. Also src/platform sets CMP0156 NEW (CMake 3.29+), so the llamatron link line no longer repeats static libraries and Apple's ld stops warning 'ignoring duplicate libraries'. Clean export: macos-app presets 4/4 with zero build warnings; native ctest -LE 'oracle|dosbox' 45/45, web 36/36

events.title: W2 M7: Llamatron.app is self-contained and runs without Homebrew. macos/bundle_dylibs.cmake (run while llamatron_macos_app builds) copies every non-system dylib the executable loads into Contents/Frameworks and points the load commands and install names at @executable_path/../Frameworks. Homebrew's SDL2 is sdl2-compat, which dlopens SDL3 trying @loader_path/libSDL3.dylib first, so libSDL3.dylib is taken from the copy's own rpath and put beside it. Rpaths leading out of the app go (the executable's /opt/homebrew/lib and sdl2-compat's ../opt/sdl3/lib), and the copies are signed ad hoc before the app. New ctests: macos_app_self_contained (macos/check_bundle.cmake: every Mach-O file in the app loads only /usr/lib, /System and its own Frameworks, no rpath points outside, codesign --verify --deep --strict passes) and macos_app_bundled_sdl (the app under DYLD_PRINT_LIBRARIES=1 loads libSDL2 and libSDL3 from Contents/Frameworks, and nothing under /opt/homebrew or /usr/local). LLAMA_SDL2_SHARED records the shared-vs-static choice for packaging. README updated

W2 M5: mixer output against the card. tests/oracle/test_snd_mixer.py (oracle.snd_mixer, 11 s) compares every output byte snd.c renders with what a Sound Blaster plays under the original sblaster.bin: sb_driver.py now keeps DMA channel 1's address (02h after the 0Ch flip-flop clear) and page (83h), so each DSP 14h transfer knows its bytes, holds each for (256 - tc) us, is cut by D0h, and leaves 80h between transfers; card_output samples that at k * 1e6 / rate us, as snd.c does. 10 random sequences x 300 ticks (test_snd_driver's calls) at 22050 (the shell's rate), 44100, 48000, 11025 and 8000 Hz, plus every sample played whole at each rate index, including sample 20 crossing the DMA page at 80000h and sample 30 crossing the one at 90000h (second halves from the IRQ handler 0511h). Output is unsigned 8-bit with no volume scaling, matching SDL's AUDIO_U8 mono. Both sides pad sample 30's tail past llatron.spl with silence (DEVIATIONS #1). events.title: W2 M5: whole-game sound lockstep. tests/oracle/test_whole_game_sound.py runs game86 with the original sblaster.bin + llatron.spl (read at run time) in whole_game.py's lockstep: PSP:89h = 0Ch and PSP:8Ah..8Dh = the driver at 7000:0000, so every CALLF [0400] (AH=3/4/5/6 and the INT 08 handler's AH=2 at 1000:3e02) runs the original driver, and the card's IRQ (04FAh) comes at its exact time before the tick or frame it precedes. The port starts with sound on, runs snd_tick before game_tick and snd_set_phase(tick phase) before game_frame, as the shell does. After every tick and frame, the original's AH=3 calls (AL, CL, CH) equal game_sound_play's log, and [B2] [B3] [B8] [2AE] [2AF] [2B0] equal snd_driver_state(). walk_vga, death_continue, warp (the 065d busy wait polls 73 times), game_over_hiscore (the 0924 wait polls 434 times, with one page-split IRQ start) and two_player all match; dropping the phase or the IRQ delivery fails at tick 260. whole_game.py (agreed with Sentinel): OriginalGame(sound_driver=), PortGame(sound=), run_lockstep(sound=) and Clock.tick_phase(); the defaults keep the stub driver, and walk_vga/warp are unchanged. sb_driver.irqs_until puts the registers back after the handler

before.name: Swift64 v0.4.2 Apple Silicon application
before.notes: The universal release was packaged and run to BASIC READY on Apple Silicon. User-supplied BASIC, KERNAL and character ROMs are required; 1541 media/ROM support varies by mode. No CPU-generation or RAM minimum is stated.

before.name: Fractalus and Void Trader: selected classic AGA builds
before.notes: Both selected builds use -m68020, explicit AGA 320x256x8bpp and v39 OS libraries. No minimum RAM or measured performance threshold is established. 64 KiB stack requests are not RAM minima.

before.name: Fractalus and Void Trader: PPC OS4 variants
before.notes: ARCH=ppc selects -mcpu=440 and newlib with sam460ex/QEMU intent. The PPC variants use silent audio stubs; Fractalus uses graphics.library fallback rendering. before.name: Mode 7 Q8 fast accelerated-emulation qualification
before.notes: Upstream recommends Q8 only above 20 MHz and measured the public rotating cube with Turbo6510 at 64 MHz: 6.95 PAL / 7.25 NTSC views per second for the fast profile versus 3.10 / 3.20 for standard. This is scene-specific emulator evidence, not a minimum, an 8-FPS guarantee or physical-hardware qualification.

after.name: Q8 accelerated-emulation qualification
after.notes: Upstream recommends Q8 only above 20 MHz. v1.8.0 reports Turbo6510 64 MHz measurements on public PAL cube scenes: Mode 2 precise/hybrid 23.70/25.05 FPS, Mode 5 27.00/27.45 FPS, and distant-cube Mode 7 standard/fast/fast+LOD 3.10/6.95/11.50 FPS. These are scene-specific emulator measurements, not minima, general guarantees or physical-hardware qualification.
